items.title: Information units and logarithm-base convention

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.2, printed pp. 18–20; zero convention and nats/bits.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–12; base-2 entropy convention and conversion to nats.

items.statement_or_definition: Use natural logarithms and nats by default. For b>1, log_b(t)=ln(t)/ln(b); base 2 gives bits. Base-b versions replace ln by log_b and retain 0 log 0=0 and +infinity for positive mass over zero reference mass.
proof_obligations: State the domain t>0 and justify ln(b)>0 for b>1 from the published logarithm order law; keep finite support and extended-real conventions explicit.

items.title: Marginals and positive-mass conditionals of a finite joint law are probability vectors

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 18–24; finite joint pmfs and their marginals.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–12; conditional pmfs and finite entropy.

items.statement_or_definition: For a finite joint pmf p(x,y), its marginals p_X and p_Y are pmfs. If p_Y(y)>0, then x↦p(x,y)/p_Y(y) is a pmf; zero-mass conditioning values are omitted.
proof_obligations: Verify nonnegativity and normalization of marginals and conditionals by finite sums; handle zero conditioning mass explicitly.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; only finite sums are rearranged.

items.title: Finite KL divergence agrees with measurable-space KL

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp. 21–23; finite divergence; Chapter 5, §5.2, printed pp. 83–89; Radon–Nikodym representation.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.1, printed pp. 21–22; discrete KL support convention and RN definition.

items.statement_or_definition: For probability vectors p,q on a finite set, the measurable KL of their full-power-set laws equals the finite sum from def-qa-35, including +infinity exactly when p_i>0=q_i for some i.
proof_obligations: Construct the finite Radon–Nikodym density explicitly in the absolutely continuous case; handle support failure separately; state that AC is invoked only through the current general KL definition.
items.axiom_use: Assumes AC only to invoke the published general measurable KL definition; the finite density and sum calculation are explicit and choice-free.

items.title: Finite log-sum inequality with support and equality cases

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp. 21–22; finite divergence inequality and Jensen route; Chapter 5, §5.2, partition/data-processing arguments.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.1 and 2.5, printed pp. 21–22, 31–35; KL support and finite data processing.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite nonnegative vectors a,b, with A=Σa_i and B=Σb_i, Σ_{a_i>0}a_i ln(a_i/b_i)≥A ln(A/B), with 0 log 0=0, positive-over-zero terms +infinity, and right side 0 when A=0. For A,B>0 equality holds exactly when a_i=(A/B)b_i for every i.
proof_obligations: Prove strict convexity of t ln t on [0,infinity), apply finite Jensen after normalization, and handle A=0, B=0, support failure, zero coordinates, and equality explicitly.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; finite Jensen and finite sums are choice-free.

items.title: Finite conditional entropy

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 35–36; conditional entropy as an average over positive-mass conditional pmfs.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–12; conditional entropy for finite X and discrete Y.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y with joint pmf p, H(X|Y)=Σ_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)H(p_{X|Y=y}), using def-qa-35 in nats. Terms at zero-mass y are omitted.
proof_obligations: State that the conditional vectors are pmfs by the local marginal/conditional lemma and that all sums are finite; never define conditional entropy by subtracting possibly infinite quantities.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all alphabets are finite.

items.title: Finite mutual information

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 36–37; finite mutual information as joint KL and entropy difference.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.1, printed pp. 41–43; mutual information as D(P_XY||P_XP_Y).

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y with joint pmf p, define I(X;Y)=D(p_XY||p_X⊗p_Y)=Σ_{p(x,y)>0}p(x,y)ln[p(x,y)/(p_X(x)p_Y(y))]. The sum is finite because positive joint mass forces positive marginals.
proof_obligations: Use the finite marginal lemma to verify every ratio on positive joint support is positive and finite; prove the entropy identity separately.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all distributions and sums are finite.

items.title: Finite conditional mutual information

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 40–41; finite CMI as conditional-product divergence.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.4, printed pp. 50–52; CMI and conditional independence.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y,Z, define I(X;Y|Z)=Σ_{z:p_Z(z)>0}p_Z(z)D(p_{XY|z}||p_{X|z}⊗p_{Y|z}); zero-mass z terms are omitted.
proof_obligations: Use the local finite conditional-pmf lemma to establish well-defined conditional distributions; prove nonnegativity, the entropy identity, and equality characterization as a separate theorem.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; every conditional sum is finite.

items.title: Finite KL divergence is nonnegative with equality exactly at equal laws

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp. 21–23, Theorem 2.3.1; finite divergence inequality and equality.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.1, printed pp. 42–43; nonnegativity and equality of mutual information via KL.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite probability vectors p,q, D(p||q)≥0 and D(p||q)=0 iff p=q; D(p||q)=+infinity if p is not absolutely continuous with respect to q.
proof_obligations: Apply log-sum with A=B=1 in the absolutely continuous case; use the exact equality case; handle support failure separately.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the argument is entirely finite.

items.title: Finite information quantities convert by the logarithm base

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.2, printed pp. 18–20; nats and bits conventions.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–12; entropy conventions and base-2 units.

items.statement_or_definition: For b>1, H_b(p)=H(p)/ln b and D_b(p||q)=D(p||q)/ln b in extended reals. The same conversion holds for finite conditional entropy, mutual information, and conditional mutual information; b=2 measures bits.
proof_obligations: Derive conversion term by term; prove ln b>0; treat support failure so +infinity remains +infinity and never subtract infinities.

items.title: Finite conditional mutual information identities and equality

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 40–41, Lemma 2.5.5; CMI nonnegativity, equality, and conditional independence.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.4, printed pp. 50–52; CMI and conditional independence.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y,Z, I(X;Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|Z)-H(X,Y|Z)≥0, with equality iff X and Y are independent under every conditional law given a positive-mass z.
proof_obligations: Expand each conditional KL as a finite sum, apply finite KL equality coordinatewise, and weight only positive-mass z values.

items.title: Finite entropy and mutual-information chain rules

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.3 and 2.5, printed pp. 24, 35–42; finite entropy and information chain rules.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 11–13; entropy chain rule; Chapter 3, §3.4, pp. 50–52, mutual-information chain rule.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y,Z, H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z) and I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z). Also I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X). All terms are finite.
proof_obligations: Factor conditional pmfs only on positive-mass atoms, sum finite logarithms, and derive the mutual-information identities without extended-real subtraction.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all sums are finite.

items.title: Data processing for a finite Markov chain, with equality condition

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 40–42; finite Markov chain identity and information chain rules.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §§3.4–3.5, printed pp. 50–53; Markov chain and mutual-information DPI.

items.statement_or_definition: If finite X,Y,Z satisfy X⊥Z|Y, equivalently p(x,z|y)=p(x|y)p(z|y) for each p_Y(y)>0, then I(X;Z)≤I(X;Y), with equality iff I(X;Y|Z)=0.
proof_obligations: Expand I(X;Y,Z) in both orders, use Markov factorization to make I(X;Z|Y)=0, and use CMI nonnegativity and equality.

items.title: Finite-alphabet Fano inequality

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 4, §4.2, printed pp. 71–72, Lemma 4.2.1; the finite error-indicator proof.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.6, printed pp. 56–58, Theorem 3.12; randomized finite-alphabet estimators.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X with alphabet size m≥2, finite observation Y, and any finite estimator Xhat in the same alphabet generated from Y (X→Y→Xhat), let Pe=P[Xhat≠X] and h2(t)=−t ln t−(1−t)ln(1−t), 0 ln0=0. Then H(X|Y)≤h2(Pe)+Pe ln(m−1). For m=1, H(X|Y)=0.
proof_obligations: Handle randomized estimators through the finite Markov channel; decompose by the error indicator; bound the error-branch entropy by ln(m−1); treat Pe=0, Pe=1, and m=1.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the estimator channel and all alphabets are finite.

items.title: Fano bound for erasure and out-of-alphabet estimates

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §3.6, printed pp. 56–58; error-indicator proof method, extended here to arbitrary finite estimate alphabets.

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 4, §4.2, printed pp. 71–72; finite Fano error-indicator method.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X on m symbols, finite Y, and any finite estimator Xhat from Y, including erasure or outputs outside X, H(X|Y)≤h2(Pe)+Pe ln m. If X is uniform, (1−Pe)ln m≤I(X;Y)+h2(Pe).
proof_obligations: Repeat the error-indicator proof with at most m messages on failure; handle m=1, Pe endpoints, and randomized estimators; rearrange the uniform-prior bound.

items.title: Binary entropy and its extremizers

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 18–23; finite entropy and uniform maximizer.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.1, printed pp. 9–12, Example 1.1; binary entropy and extrema.

items.statement_or_definition: For Bernoulli(p), h(p)=−p ln p−(1−p)ln(1−p), with h(0)=h(1)=0. The unique maximum is ln2 at p=1/2; h(p)=0 exactly at p=0 or 1.
proof_obligations: Compute the KL divergence to the uniform binary law to prove the unique maximum; use the zero-term convention and strict negativity of ln on (0,1) to characterize zero entropy.

items.title: Finite KL divergence is directional and may be infinite

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.3, printed pp. 21–23; directed finite divergence and support convention.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.1, printed pp. 21–22; discrete KL support convention.

items.statement_or_definition: Refute the assertion that finite KL divergence is symmetric: for p=δ0 and q=(ε,1−ε), 0<ε<1, D(p||q)=−ln ε<∞ while D(q||p)=+∞. For disjoint point masses, both directions are +∞.
proof_obligations: Compute both directions from the finite support convention and explicitly verify the disjoint-support boundary.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all distributions are finite.

items.title: Independent and deterministic finite information

references.title: Robert M. Gray, Entropy and Information Theory, corrected first edition
references.locator: Chapter 2, §2.5, printed pp. 36–37; mutual information and deterministic dependence.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, author prepublication
references.locator: Chapter 3, §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 42–45; MI as KL and entropy reduction.

items.statement_or_definition: For finite X,Y, independence gives I(X;Y)=0; if Y=f(X), then I(X;Y)=H(Y).
proof_obligations: For independence substitute the product joint law in finite KL; for a deterministic map sum over each fiber or use H(Y|X)=0 and the finite entropy identity.
